map.summary: This area measures how good the search is. It loads versioned test bundles whose files are hash-checked, prepares each bundle into its own isolated search index, asks every test question in four search styles, compares the ranked results against human relevance labels, and writes repeatable JSON and Markdown reports. A command-line tool builds the SciFact test set. It is a command-line tool, not a service; the old debug web route is retired, and database tables for runs exist but nothing yet moves a run beyond 'queued'.
unknowns: How the scored report or saved run reaches any user-facing output is not shown; the old debug web route now returns 404.
How an on-disk bundle is loaded into the stored dataset and relevance-label tables is not shown.
Nothing here moves a stored benchmark run beyond its default 'queued' status or writes its metrics.
Whether prepared corpus work always runs inline in the command process or can also be handled by a separate worker is not traced.
The exact callers of the evaluation search boundary, and the code that writes the report stage after preparation, are inferred from tests rather than production code.

diagrams.title: How a dataset becomes a scored report
diagrams.description: A hash-verified test bundle is prepared into its own search index, every test question is searched four ways, results are scored against human relevance labels, and repeatable report files are written.

diagrams.title: How the SciFact test set is built
diagrams.description: A pinned public archive is downloaded and hash-checked, converted into the shared bundle format, trimmed to a deterministic 30-question, 500-document baseline, and re-loaded to prove it is valid.

diagrams.title: How one bundle file set is checked
diagrams.description: A bundle directory is read with its manifest, each listed file's fingerprint is recomputed and compared, then the records are parsed and cross-checked for broken or missing relevance labels.

diagrams.title: How stored evaluation records are shaped
diagrams.description: Database tables hold per-tenant dataset bundles, their relevance labels, benchmark runs, and an audit trail; the tables only store and constrain data, and the code that moves a run through its statuses is not shown.

F0001.statement: score_ranking in evaluation/metrics.py computes retrieval quality for one query: it deduplicates a ranked list of document keys before applying cutoffs, then returns recall at cutoffs 5, 10 and 50, mean reciprocal rank at 10, and nDCG at 10, using graded judgments where unjudged results receive no credit.

F0002.statement: score_ranking rejects malformed input by raising ValueError when any relevance grade is not an integer between 0 and 3, or when a query has no positive judgment, so scoring cannot proceed without at least one relevant document.

F0003.statement: EvaluationSearch in evaluation/search.py is the isolated evaluation search boundary; it is constructed with Settings, rewrites the settings to a fixed candidate/result budget of 100 (benchmark_settings), and opens its provider resources through an AsyncExitStack used as an async context manager.

F0004.statement: EvaluationSearch.search supports four modes ('bm25', 'dense', 'hybrid', 'hybrid_rerank') and raises ValueError for an unknown mode; lexical retrieval is created eagerly in __init__ while dense, hybrid and reranked retrievers are created lazily on first non-bm25 use.

F0005.statement: Each query derives its tenant, collection and document scope from the dataset, and every returned evidence item is validated against that scope (tenant, collection, document id and pipeline version); a mismatch raises ValueError, so search cannot return evidence outside the prepared evaluation scope.

F0006.statement: Evaluation metadata filters are restricted to source_type, author, source_date_from and source_date_to; any other key raises ValueError and source_date_* values are parsed through parse_source_date.

F0007.statement: EvaluationSearch returns a dict containing the mode, a per-chunk list (with rank and a mapped evaluation_document_id), a deduplicated document-level list (first chunk per document, renumbered rank) and an asdict-serialized trace from the underlying retriever.

F0008.statement: The hybrid mode flattens hybrid results to their per-item evidence, and hybrid_rerank mode flattens reranked results to their nested hybrid evidence, so all four modes converge on the same RetrievalResult evidence list shape.

F0009.statement: Test evidence shows the retired debug route POST /debug/search returns 404 from the app created by create_app(), indicating the evaluation HTTP debug endpoint is no longer served.

F0010.statement: A test exercises all four modes with fake embedding and reranking providers and a mocked OpenSearch transport; the same query in every mode returns two chunks and one deduplicated document entry, confirming per-query dedup and document roll-up behavior.

F0011.statement: Tests confirm runtime failure modes: corrupted tenant/collection in hits surfaces a RetrievalError matching 'retrieval_scope_violation', and a document id outside the prepared scope raises ValueError; unsupported filter keys and unknown modes also raise ValueError.

F0012.statement: scifact.build_subset in evaluation/scifact.py builds a deterministic SciFact subset from a source dataset directory: it is repeatable (identical output across runs and independent of input ordering), selects 30 queries chosen by SHA-256 hash of 'scifact-subset-v1:<query_id>', caps required documents at 500, and preserves all judgments for selected queries.

F0013.statement: build_subset enforces input constraints by raising ValueError when the source has fewer than 30 queries or when more than 500 documents are required by selected judgments.

F0014.statement: scifact exposes a CLI entry (scifact.main) invoked as 'scifact subset --source ...' that writes to a SUBSET_OUTPUT default location, and built subsets are registered such that selected_dataset('scifact-subset') returns the 500-document corpus.

F0015.statement: The evaluation package (evaluation/__init__.py) re-exports the versioned dataset contracts and loader: CorpusRecord, DatasetManifest, EvaluationDataset, JudgmentRecord, QueryRecord and load_dataset, defining the dataset contract surface other evaluation code imports.

F0016.statement: Inferred from test wiring rather than production code: the benchmark runner shares embedding and reranking provider resources across queries within one EvaluationSearch context without caching query embeddings, as stated in the class docstring; the concrete callers of EvaluationSearch and the report-writing stage are not shown in these excerpts.

F0017.statement: load_dataset reads a four-file dataset directory (manifest.json plus corpus.jsonl, queries.jsonl, judgments.jsonl), verifies each listed file's SHA-256 against the manifest before parsing, and rejects blank lines, non-object JSON lines, duplicate corpus/query IDs, judgments referencing unknown queries or targets, target type mismatches, queries with no judgment, and queries without any positive judgment (DatasetValidationError).

F0018.statement: The loader produces an EvaluationDataset carrying immutable validated manifest/corpus/queries/judgments plus two derived content hashes: corpus_hash (SHA-256 of corpus.jsonl only) and dataset_hash (SHA-256 over schema version, dataset id, version, and sorted per-file hashes), which later serve as the identity inputs for scope derivation.

F0019.statement: selected_dataset maps three fixed names ('synthetic-workspace', 'scifact', 'scifact-subset') to local dataset directories and raises ValueError for unknown names; it delegates to load_dataset.

F0020.statement: evaluation_scope derives a deterministic, reusable EvaluationScope: all evaluation data lives under a fixed EVALUATION_TENANT UUID, the collection id is uuid5(EVALUATION_TENANT, corpus_hash + ':' + pipeline_version), and each document id is uuid5(collection_id, record.id), so identical corpus+config reproduces the same identifiers. It rejects non-document corpus records.

F0021.statement: evaluation_index_settings renames the OpenSearch read/write aliases to 'hybrid-rag-eval-<collection_id>-read/-write' (via settings.model_copy) so evaluation indexes are isolated from demo aliases and manual rebuilds; ensure_evaluation_index HEADs the physical index and, on 404 only, creates it with OpenSearchIndexManager and points/promotes the aliases. A non-404 response is raised.

F0022.statement: prepare_corpus is the orchestrator: it applies the isolated index settings, ensures the index exists, then within one DB transaction inserts the evaluation Tenant and Collection idempotently (on_conflict_do_nothing), and finally disposes the async engine and advances to corpus compaction and verification. document_delay must be nonnegative.

F0023.statement: For each corpus record, prepare_corpus builds content from title + text, computes its SHA-256, saves it via LocalFileStorage at a tenant/document-derived key, and inserts a Document row (recording source_metadata including evaluation_id) only if not already present. If a stored document exists with a different content_hash or metadata, it raises 'Prepared evaluation document differs from dataset' to enforce bundle immutability.

F0024.statement: Document ingestion for evaluation reuses the durable pipeline: IngestionJobService.enqueue_document is called per document, and only when the job did not already succeed does the code run it inline via run_configured_job with a ManualActor (synchronous CLI actor) and a ManualPublisher that does nothing; a non-SUCCEEDED JobRunResult raises. This means evaluation preparation executes durable jobs inline in the CLI process, not through a separate worker.

F0025.statement: compact_corpus force-merges the physical evaluation index to one segment with flush=true (HTTP _forcemerge) to settle deleted promotion records before benchmarking a completed static corpus.

F0026.statement: verify_prepared fails closed: it counts succeeded IngestionJob rows for the scope's tenant/documents/pipeline_version and requires exactly one per corpus record, validates that each job's checkpoint.index receipt holds a string generation_id and integer chunk_count, then aggregates the OpenSearch read alias by document_id and generation_id and requires the live index to match the expected generation and chunk count exactly; otherwise it raises 'rebuild before running'. It returns the total chunk count.

F0027.statement: The preparation flow's external systems are PostgreSQL (via async SQLAlchemy engine from async_database_url), OpenSearch (via httpx for index existence/forcemerge/search and OpenSearchIndexManager/OpenSearchDocumentIndex for index operations), and local file storage; result is the returned EvaluationScope acting as a set of stable identifiers consumed by later search/scoring and reporting steps.

F0028.statement: Dataset contracts are strict and frozen (extra fields forbidden) with constrained types: identifiers must match a lowercase slug pattern, hashes must be 64 hex chars, corpus records are either 'document' or 'chunk' (chunks require document_id, documents must not have one), and judgment relevance grades are 0-3.

F0029.statement: The manifest requires schema_version 'evaluation-dataset-v1', purpose 'evaluation', and must list the three data files exactly once each; loading reads all files into memory and hashes them before validation, so failures occur before any mutation of the directory.

F0030.statement: How prepare_corpus's returned scope and the verified index are consumed by the search/metrics/reporting code in the changed files (metrics.py, search.py) is not shown in these excerpts; the boundary from prepared corpus to scored report is inferred from the module docstring and neighboring summaries.

F0031.statement: The evaluation runner is a command-line tool (main() with argparse subcommands prepare/run/compare/export) that a person starts to build retrieval benchmarks; it is not a service.

F0032.statement: evaluate() is the core scoring loop: for each dataset query it runs every search mode, records each mode's metrics, elapsed time, chunk and document counts, and the full search result, then compares each mode against bm25 as a reference.

F0033.statement: evaluate() assembles per-query judgments from dataset.judgments, requiring one unique document judgment per query per target and rejecting duplicates or non-document targets with ValueError.

F0034.statement: The scoring path calls score_ranking(ranking, judgments[query.id]) over a list of document_id values, and per-query deltas versus the bm25 mode are computed as metric differences.

F0035.statement: Aggregate metrics are the arithmetic mean of each per-query metric across all queries, keyed by search mode.

F0036.statement: run_baseline() orchestrates a full reproducible run: it loads benchmark settings, selects the dataset, applies evaluation index settings, verifies the prepared corpus, determines evaluation scope, then runs the search evaluation.

F0037.statement: run_baseline() contacts OpenSearch over HTTP (httpx.AsyncClient against settings.opensearch_url) to fetch the read alias /_alias/{settings.opensearch_read_alias} and records the sorted index names in report metadata.

F0038.statement: run_baseline() shells out to git rev-parse HEAD and git diff HEAD --name-only to record the code revision and a dirty-worktree flag in the report metadata, making runs traceable to a code state.

F0039.statement: Report metadata captures dataset identity and hashes (dataset_id, version, dataset_hash, corpus_hash, document/query counts), pipeline version, tenant and collection ids, hardware info, cache state, query delay, execution description, model names, adapters, metric rules, and a count of hybrid_rerank fallbacks.

F0040.statement: save_report() writes two files into an output directory: report.json (jsonable_encoder-serialized, indented, sorted keys) and report.md generated by markdown_report().

F0041.statement: markdown_report() renders a human-readable version with aggregate scores and per-query differences against BM25, and notes that unjudged documents earn zero credit.

F0042.statement: compare_reports() enforces comparability between two reports by requiring equal dataset, configuration, pipeline_version, index, models, adapters, and identical query-id sequences, raising ValueError otherwise, then reports maximum per-query and aggregate metric drift while treating latency as descriptive only.

F0043.statement: configuration() uses an explicit allowlist of settings fields (opensearch_bm25_* plus a fixed set) to prevent credentials and unrelated settings from entering reports, and hardcodes rrf_rank_constant to 60.

F0044.statement: The run subcommand requires an output path and a --cache-state string (described in help as an honest description of observed cache conditions), and optionally a --query-delay that evaluate() validates as nonnegative and uses as an asyncio.sleep between queries.

F0045.statement: The prepare subcommand runs prepare_corpus() for a selected dataset, with an optional --document-delay; export re-serializes an existing report JSON into JSON and Markdown outputs, and compare prints a JSON drift summary for two report files.

F0046.statement: In evaluate(), before scoring, each returned chunk is stripped to only chunk_id, evaluation_document_id, rank, and score, avoiding duplicating source bytes across many benchmark queries.

F0047.statement: SciFact evaluation module is a command-line tool (S0009 main) with three subcommands: download (fetch the pinned archive and convert it), subset (build a deterministic baseline subset from a converted dataset), and validate (load and summarize an existing dataset directory); the command prints a one-line summary with counts and hashes.

F0048.statement: download_archive fetches the fixed BEIR SciFact URL over HTTP with redirects followed, writes to a '.partial' temp file, then verifies the whole archive SHA-256 against a hard-coded pin and only then renames it into place; a mismatch raises ValueError and the temp file is always deleted.

F0049.statement: convert_archive re-verifies the pinned hash of the local archive, unzips it in memory, reads qrels/test.tsv plus corpus.jsonl and queries.jsonl, and writes a shared three-file contract (corpus.jsonl, queries.jsonl, judgments.jsonl) plus a manifest with schema_version evaluation-dataset-v1, dataset_id 'scifact', source license, and per-file SHA-256.

F0050.statement: Conversion re-keys identifiers with prefixes ('scifact-doc-', 'scifact-query-'), keeps only queries that appear in qrels, maps qrels score>0 to relevance_grade 3 and 0 otherwise, and sorts all output by id, so the result is a deterministic, reproducible bundle.

F0051.statement: build_subset selects 30 queries and 500 documents using a stable salted SHA-256 ordering ('scifact-subset-v1:<id>'), takes all judgments for the chosen queries, fills the corpus to 500 via the same ordering, refuses to proceed if the source has fewer than 30 queries or 500 documents or if judgments need more than 500 documents, and re-runs load_dataset on its own output as a validation step.

F0052.statement: The SciFact subset manifest derives from the parent dataset manifest but overrides dataset_id, name, version ('scifact-subset-v1') and description, recording the parent dataset hash and the exact selection rule so the subset is self-describing.

F0053.statement: S0009 depends on hybrid_rag_search.evaluation.datasets (StrictModel, load_dataset) for parsing/validating bundles and on httpx for the download; these are observed imports whose runtime behavior is only partially executed here (load_dataset is called for output validation).

F0054.statement: S0010 defines SQLAlchemy ORM tables for the evaluation subsystem: evaluation_datasets, judgments, evaluation_runs, and audit_events, all keyed by tenant_id and mostly using composite (tenant_id, id) constraints and foreign keys.

F0055.statement: EvaluationDataset stores a named versioned dataset per tenant with a required SHA-256 corpus_hash (regex-checked), free-text description, arbitrary JSONB metadata constrained to be an object, and unique (tenant_id, name, version).

F0056.statement: Judgment stores a query (key and text) and a target (type 'document' or 'chunk', id) with relevance_grade constrained to 0..3, optional expected_answer, JSONB key_facts (array) and metadata_filters (object), unique per tenant/dataset/query/target, and cascades when its dataset is deleted.

F0057.statement: EvaluationRun links a dataset and a retrieval config (both per-tenant foreign keys with RESTRICT delete) plus a non-negative seed, carries a status constrained to queued/running/succeeded/failed/cancelled, JSONB metrics (object), optional error_message, started_at/finished_at timestamps and created/updated timestamps; it defaults to 'queued'.

F0058.statement: AuditEvent records tenant-scoped actions with optional actor membership (composite FK to memberships), a namespaced action pattern like 'resource.verb', an entity type/id, JSONB details, and an occurred_at timestamp; referenced rows are protected by RESTRICT deletes.

F0059.statement: JudgmentTarget and EvaluationRunStatus are StrEnum symbol tables mirroring the database CHECK constraints for target type and run status, acting as the in-code vocabulary for those allowed values.

F0060.statement: The database layer is PostgreSQL-specific (JSONB, UUID dialect types, regex CHECK constraints, jsonb_typeof), so this schema cannot run on SQLite without adaptation.

F0061.statement: There is no code here that transitions an EvaluationRun from queued to running/succeeded or writes metrics; the models only provide storage and constraints, so the runtime orchestration of runs is not evidenced in this batch.

F0062.statement: How a converted on-disk bundle (S0009 output) is loaded into the EvaluationDataset/Judgment database tables is not shown in these excerpts; the two representations (files with hashes, rows with ids/hashes) are parallel but the linking code is absent.

F0063.statement: The evaluation area is exercised mainly through tests of its public functions: prepare_corpus, verify_prepared, ensure_evaluation_index, compact_corpus, load_dataset, score_ranking, evaluate, compare_reports, save_report, and run_baseline. These tests reveal implemented behavior but the production code bodies are not shown. This is inferred.

F0064.statement: prepare_corpus prepares a dataset corpus into storage: it creates an ingestion job per corpus document via IngestionJobService.enqueue_document, runs it with run_configured_job, saves a document record (session.add) whose id is uuid5(scope.collection_id, record.id), and stores the document text through LocalFileStorage. It returns a scope with a collection_id used to derive those ids.

F0065.statement: prepare_corpus reuses durable jobs: when session.get returns an already-succeeded job, the document is not re-enqueued and session.add is not called again. This makes preparation idempotent across repeated runs.

F0066.statement: prepare_corpus validates preparation and raises ValueError when a stored document's content_hash differs from the stored file's SHA-256, when an ingestion job's run result is RETRY_SCHEDULED, and when document_delay is negative. document_delay greater than zero causes a sleep between documents, pacing work.

F0067.statement: verify_prepared confirms the dataset is ready by loading each scoped document's IngestionJob, requiring a checkpoint with index.generation_id and chunk_count, querying OpenSearch aggregations for each document's generations, and returning the document count (16 in the test). It raises ValueError when no jobs exist ("not prepared"), when a checkpoint receipt is missing, or when the observed index generation differs from the recorded one.

F0068.statement: ensure_evaluation_index creates an isolated OpenSearch index for a dataset using OpenSearchIndexManager, calling create, point_write_alias, and promote_read_alias, and is idempotent: if the index already exists (HTTP 200 rather than 404) create is not called again. The evaluation read alias is namespaced with a prefix like "hybrid-rag-eval-".

F0069.statement: ManualActor and ManualPublisher are minimal helpers used to inject documents in tests: ManualActor.send returns its argument unchanged, send_with_options forwards args, and ManualPublisher.publish accepts a uuid without side effects. Their production role is not shown.

F0070.statement: load_dataset reads a versioned dataset bundle from a directory, verifying every listed file against its SHA-256 in manifest.json and producing a deterministic EvaluationDataset (same input yields equal output). The synthetic-workspace v1 bundle holds 8 corpus documents and 12 queries across categories exact-match, paraphrase, stale-version, and conflicting-evidence, with a fixed corpus_hash.

F0071.statement: load_dataset enforces data contracts and raises DatasetValidationError for: a file whose hash does not match the manifest, malformed JSON lines, blank lines, judgments referencing unknown queries or targets, judgment target type mismatch, duplicate query IDs, queries lacking any judgment, queries lacking a positive (grade > 0) judgment, and an invalid manifest. It also fails when a listed file is missing or unreadable.

F0072.statement: CorpusRecord and DatasetManifest are contract types: a chunk record must carry a document_id and a document record must not, and a manifest must list the expected set of files. Violations raise pydantic ValidationError.

F0073.statement: score_ranking computes graded ranking metrics (recall@5, recall@10, recall@50, mrr@10, ndcg@10) from an ordered result list and a map of target id to relevance grade. Duplicates are removed before applying cutoffs, short result lists keep the full denominator, unjudged results never count as hits, and empty rankings score all zeros.

F0074.statement: score_ranking rejects invalid judgment grades, raising ValueError for grades of 0, negative numbers, values above 3, and boolean values.

F0075.statement: evaluate runs every dataset query against a caller-supplied async search function in each of the four modes (MODES), producing an aggregate report per mode plus per-query mode results with delta_vs_bm25 metrics and a search trace. It rejects duplicate judgments with ValueError and validates query_delay (rejecting negative values) while inserting a sleep of query_delay between queries.

F0076.statement: compare_reports produces a deterministic regression comparison, reporting max_absolute_per_query_metric_delta and raising ValueError when the two reports differ in models, query sets, or other metadata, which prevents comparing non-comparable runs.

F0077.statement: save_report writes a JSON report.json (including per-query per-mode deltas) and a human-readable report.md containing a "Per-query differences" section, giving both machine and reader outputs.

F0078.statement: run_baseline orchestrates an end-to-end baseline: it loads settings, verifies the prepared index via verify_prepared, captures reproduction metadata (platform, processor, code_revision from git rev-parse, tracked_worktree_dirty, cache_state, adapters, rerank_fallback_count from search traces), runs evaluate through EvaluationSearch, and saves report.json without writing secret values such as API keys. evaluation_scope derives a stable scope from dataset corpus_hash and index schema version but is independent of judgments and dataset_hash.

F0079.statement: The evaluation subsystem supports four JSONL record schemas for dataset bundles: corpus records (id, type of document or chunk, text, optional title/metadata), query records (id, text, optional category, expected answer, key facts, metadata filters), judgment records (query_id, target_type, target_id, relevance_grade integer 0-3), and a manifest tying the bundle together (dataset id, name, version, source name with optional URL/archive hash/license, and exactly three files each with a path and SHA-256). These schemas define the on-disk contract a loaded bundle must satisfy.

F0080.statement: A scifact module under the evaluation package provides a CLI (scifact.main) with 'download' and 'validate' subcommands operating on an --output dataset directory. The download command fetches and converts an archive and prints a line like 'corpus=2 queries=1 judgments=1'; the validate command prints 'dataset=scifact' and 'dataset_hash=' from the built manifest.json.

F0081.statement: scifact.download_archive(destination) performs an HTTP GET via httpx, checks the downloaded bytes against a module-level constant SCIFACT_ARCHIVE_SHA256, and returns the destination path. On hash mismatch it raises ValueError('SHA-256 mismatch') and leaves no 'scifact.partial' temp file behind, implying a partial-then-rename write strategy.

F0082.statement: scifact.convert_archive(archive, output_dir) unzips a SciFact archive containing corpus.jsonl, queries.jsonl and qrels/test.tsv, converts them into the shared dataset bundle format, and is deterministic: converting the same archive to two different destinations yields bundles that load equal via load_dataset.

F0083.statement: The conversion renames SciFact identifiers into a namespaced scheme: corpus doc ids become 'scifact-doc-<id>' and query ids become 'scifact-query-<id>'; converted records sort predictably (doc ids ordered as scifact-doc-10 then scifact-doc-20) and queries are deduplicated to those that have judgments (only scifact-query-1 appeared when two were in the source).

F0084.statement: SciFact qrels integer scores are not copied verbatim; score 1 is mapped to relevance_grade 3 in the produced judgment, implying a grade-mapping step rather than a direct pass-through.

F0085.statement: scifact._summary(output_dir) produces textual summary content containing a version marker like 'version=beir-2021-03-19-test-v1', and the built manifest.json records both a dataset hash and a source.archive_sha256 field whose value is the SHA-256 of the original archive.

F0086.statement: The dataset bundle loader load_dataset(path) reads a converted bundle directory and returns an object exposing .corpus, .queries and .judgments collections; each corpus/query record has an id, each judgment has a relevance_grade, and two independently converted bundles can be compared for structural and value equality with ==.

F0087.statement: The tagline 'beir-2021-03-19-test-v1' in the generated summary shows SciFact is treated as a BEIR-family dataset version, so bundles carry a version string identifying the upstream snapshot they came from.

F0088.statement: Corpus records may be either 'document' type or 'chunk' type, and judgments carry a target_type of the same enum, allowing evaluation labels to point at whole documents or at chunks produced by the ingestion stage.

F0089.statement: All identifiers across corpus, query, judgment and manifest records must match the pattern '^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*$', so scores are always keyed by lower-case slug identifiers. The 'scifact-doc-10' style names observed in tests conform to this.

F0090.statement: The manifest schema requires exactly three file descriptors (minItems=maxItems=3) with paths drawn from the enum corpus.jsonl, queries.jsonl, judgments.jsonl and an SHA-256 per file, plus a required purpose field fixed to the constant 'evaluation' and schema_version fixed to 'evaluation-dataset-v1'.

F0091.statement: The manifest schema is strict: additionalProperties is false at the top level and inside the source object, so extra metadata not in the schema will cause validation to fail. The source object requires at least a name and otherwise accepts url, archive_sha256 (64 lowercase hex) and license, all nullable.

F0092.statement: The query record schema supports optional fields beyond id and text: category, expected_answer, key_facts array, and metadata_filters object, which are the hooks for question-level evaluation and filter-based retrieval testing.

F0093.statement: The tests use monkeypatch to substitute scifact.httpx.get and scifact.download_archive, confirming that network fetching is isolated behind these two names so the CLI can be exercised without live HTTP. They also patch sys.argv to drive scifact.main for both subcommands.

F0094.statement: The corpus and query schemas require a non-empty text (minLength 1) and a valid id, so any SciFact record with empty text or an invalid id would be rejected at load/validation time rather than silently stored.
